notice: SYNTHETIC RECORDS. Made up by radar/declarations/generate.py from a seed, to show what the radar's restricted layer would do with export declarations. No record is or describes a real declaration, exporter, consignee, forwarder or agent; the ids are made up and look nothing like EORI numbers; there are no names, addresses or postcodes.
house_line: A rise in exports is a lead, not evidence of a breach.
about: The restricted layer's detectors: one per pattern, each citing the red flags it implements (radar/brief/spec/redflags.json, where each red flag's official source is cited). A detector puts out questions for a person to check, never findings. Thresholds are ours, set on synthetic data [Guessing].

radar_codes.854231: Electronic integrated circuits: processors and controllers
radar_codes.851762: Machines for the reception, conversion and transmission of voice, images or other data
radar_codes.8548: Electrical parts of machinery or apparatus not elsewhere specified

scope.flagged_routes_source: routes shown as a lead or a watch item in demo/radar/leads.json when this layer was built (run of October 2026)
scope.neighbouring_codes_note: A neighbouring code is in the same heading and outside the radar's nine; whether it is controlled is not modelled [Certain].

detectors.name: new-corridor-consignee
detectors.title: New consignee in a corridor buying the radar's goods

implements.question: Is the customer new to importing or exporting goods on the Common High Priority Items List?
Is the destination, or any country the goods pass through, one that the UK guidance names for enhanced due diligence?

then_check.question: Do the goods fall within the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?
Is the customer new, and was it incorporated outside the UK after 24 February 2022 with a line of business in military or dual-use goods?
Have the customer and its known directors been checked against the UK Sanctions List?
Does the customer have a business history and a web presence that fit the order?
Who is the end user, and can an end-user certificate be provided and checked?

detectors.mapping: new-chpl-trader [Likely]: the declarations show a consignee new to receiving these goods from UK exporters, not new to importing them from anywhere. transit-edd-country [Certain] where the destination is one the UK guidance names; Georgia, Azerbaijan and Tajikistan are not named, so for them the detector cites only new-chpl-trader.

wording.question: Is {consignee} in {country} new to buying goods on the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?
wording.basis: First seen in a UK export declaration on {first_seen}. In the last 12 months: {value} of the radar's goods in {shipments} shipments from {exporters}.

detectors.name: route-volume-jump
detectors.title: An exporter's exports jumping on a route the public radar shows

implements.question: Have an existing customer's orders risen in volume or value beyond its usual pattern, and is there a business reason for the rise?

then_check.question: Do the goods fall within the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?
Has the customer given clear details of the end user, the intended end use and its own ownership when asked?
Do the goods and their capabilities fit the buyer's and the end user's line of business?
Is the customer open about where the goods will end up and what they are for?

detectors.mapping: order-volume-rise [Likely]: the guidance speaks of an existing customer's orders; the detector sees one exporter's declared exports on one route and names the consignees behind the rise.

thresholds.routes: routes the public radar shows as a lead or a watch item

wording.question: Have {exporter}'s exports of {code} ({code_desc}) to {country} risen beyond their usual pattern, and is there a business reason for the rise?
wording.basis: {value_w} in the last 12 months against {value_p} in the 12 before ({ratio} times), on a route the public radar shows as {status}. {consignees} behind the rise, {new} of them first seen in the last 12 months.

detectors.name: shared-party
detectors.title: A consignee or forwarder shared by unrelated exporters

implements.question: Is the consignee a business that would use the goods, rather than a bank, a mail centre or a logistics firm?
Does the customer share its address with many other businesses dealing in similar goods, or trade from a residential address?

then_check.question: Is a freight forwarder named as the final destination of the goods?
Does the customer have a business history and a web presence that fit the order?
Do the goods and their capabilities fit the buyer's and the end user's line of business?
Is the shipping route clear and usual for these goods and this destination, or complex and through several third countries?

detectors.mapping: consignee-uses-goods [Likely]: a consignee supplied by many unrelated exporters may be a forwarder or logistics firm rather than a user of the goods. shared-address [Guessing]: the guidance's indicator is an address shared by many businesses; the declarations' nearest parallel is one party shared by many exporters. A deployment holding the consignee's name and address (DE 3/9) could test the address itself; the synthetic records hold no addresses.

wording.question: Is {party} in {country} a business that would use these goods, rather than a forwarder or logistics firm, and why do exporters in {groups} different ownership groups send it goods on the Common High Priority Items List?
wording.question_forwarder: Why do exporters in {groups} different ownership groups send goods on the Common High Priority Items List to {countries} through {party}, and is a forwarder named as the final destination on any of these shipments?
wording.basis: In the last 24 months: {shipments} shipments of the radar's goods from {exporters} in {groups} ownership groups. First seen in a UK export declaration on {first_seen}.
wording.basis_forwarder: In the last 24 months: {items} goods items of the radar's goods to corridor countries through {party}, {share} of everything declared with it, from {exporters} in {groups} ownership groups. First declared on {first_seen}.

detectors.name: unit-value
detectors.title: Declared values per kilogram far out of line for the code

implements.question: Is the customer paying well above the market price, or are invoices split so that each stays under a control limit?
Are the goods recorded under the correct HS code on every document?

then_check.question: Has the customer given clear details of the end user, the intended end use and its own ownership when asked?
Do the goods and their capabilities fit the buyer's and the end user's line of business?

detectors.mapping: price-and-invoices [Likely]: a value per kilogram far above the code's norm is one way a price well above the market shows in declarations. hs-code-check [Likely]: a value per kilogram far from the norm can mean the goods are not what the code describes.

thresholds.scope: corridor destinations; the norm for each code is taken over every destination

wording.question: Why is the declared value per kilogram of {code} ({code_desc}) from {exporter} to {consignee} in {country} {factor} the usual for the code, and are the goods recorded under the correct code and at the market price?
wording.basis: {outliers} of {items} goods items are more than 3.5 robust deviations from the code's median of {norm} per kg; this pair's median is {pair} per kg.

detectors.name: code-switch
detectors.title: A code switching to a neighbouring code outside the radar's nine

implements.question: Are the goods recorded under the correct HS code on every document?

then_check.question: Do the goods and their capabilities fit the buyer's and the end user's line of business?
Has the customer given clear details of the end user, the intended end use and its own ownership when asked?
Do the goods fall within the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?

detectors.mapping: hs-code-check [Likely]: the guidance lists goods recorded under a code that is not subject to controls; the detector sees the same flow move to a neighbouring code at a similar value per kilogram. Whether the neighbouring code is controlled is not modelled.

wording.question: Why did {exporter}'s shipments to {consignee} in {country} move from {code_a} to {code_b} at a similar value per kilogram, and are the goods recorded under the correct code on every document?
wording.basis: {n_a} goods items under {code_a} ({desc_a}) up to {last_a}; {n_b} under {code_b} ({desc_b}) from {first_b}. Median value per kg {uv_a}, then {uv_b}.

detectors.name: russia-switch
detectors.title: Exports to Russia stopping after 24 February 2022 and moving to a corridor

implements.question: Did the customer start receiving these goods only after 24 February 2022, or receive far more of them since then?
Is the destination, or any country the goods pass through, one that the UK guidance names for enhanced due diligence?

then_check.question: Has the way these goods are shipped to this customer changed since sanctions were imposed?
Does the customer have business ties to a sanctioned person or entity, or a branch office in Russia?
Do the goods fall within the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?
Who is the end user, and can an end-user certificate be provided and checked?

detectors.mapping: chpl-orders-since-2022 [Likely]: the indicator is a customer that started receiving these goods only after 24 February 2022; the detector tests that for the consignees that took the place of the exporter's Russia trade. transit-edd-country [Certain] where a destination is one the UK guidance names.

wording.question: Did {exporter}'s customers in {countries} start receiving these goods only after 24 February 2022, when its exports of them to Russia stopped, and has the way the goods are shipped changed?
wording.basis: {ru_value} of the radar's goods to Russia from January 2021 to 23 February 2022; {corr_value} in the two years from March 2022 to {consignees} in {countries} first seen after 24 February 2022. Codes in common: {codes}.

detectors.name: small-frequent
detectors.title: Small, frequent shipments to one consignee

implements.question: Are the goods going out in small, frequent shipments to one central location, such as a warehouse in a third country, where they are combined into one shipment?

then_check.question: Is the customer paying well above the market price, or are invoices split so that each stays under a control limit?
Is the consignee a business that would use the goods, rather than a bank, a mail centre or a logistics firm?
Are delivery dates or destinations vague, or are several third-country freight forwarders used on one transaction?

detectors.mapping: small-frequent-shipments [Certain]: the indicator names small, frequent shipments to a central location; what counts as small and frequent is ours [Guessing].

wording.question: Are the goods going to {consignee} in {country} in small, frequent shipments to one central location, and are orders or invoices being split to stay under a limit?
wording.basis: {shipments} shipments of the radar's goods in the last 12 months, median {value} and {mass} kg, from {exporters}.

cases.grouping: Signals that share an exporter and destination, or a consignee, go into one case. A case raised by two or more detectors is listed as check first; any other as check. No case carries a score.
cases.graph: Each case's parties plus one hop, at most 25 neighbours per party.
